input_text: Web API on AKS with 3 Standard_D4s_v5 nodes, Azure SQL Database General Purpose 4 vCore provisioned, Redis Premium P1 cache, all in West Europe. About 2,000 users, busy in business hours, quiet at night. Data must stay in the EU.

components.details: Web API hosted on AKS; cluster tier assumed Standard since not stated otherwise
3 AKS worker nodes, Standard_D4s_v5, serving the Web API; busy in business hours, quiet at night
General Purpose tier, provisioned compute, 4 vCore

constraints.notes: About 2,000 users; load is high in business hours and low at night. Data must stay in the EU.

Premium P1 cache, whole-cache meter, one instance, billed all month

options.details: Consumption plan, Web API container, 1 vCPU 2 GiB per replica, min 2 replicas in business hours scaling to 1 at night via HTTP/cron scaling rules, EU region
options.rationale: Container Apps has no cluster management fee and no always-on node pool, and it scales replicas with load, so you pay mainly for the vCPU/memory actually used instead of 3 fixed D4s_v5 nodes plus the AKS control plane.
tradeoffs: Less Kubernetes control (no custom operators/CRDs, limited node tuning)
Migration of manifests to Container Apps config
Per-second vCPU/memory billing can exceed dedicated nodes if load is constantly high
options.effort_reason: Serverless containers with no cluster to run, but team has no Kubernetes experience so the move needs rework of deployment and scaling rules

meters.why: Assumed ~1.4 replicas on average (2 in ~10 business hours on 22 days, 1 otherwise), 1 vCPU each, all month; ~3,600,000 vCPU-seconds active, billed as active usage (conservative, ignores idle rate).
2 GiB per replica x ~3,600,000 replica-seconds = ~7.2M GiB-seconds active memory a month.
Assumed ~3 million HTTP requests a month for 2,000 users (about 70 requests per user per working day).

options.details: Linux, 2 instances (autoscale to 1 at night), Web API as container or code, EU region
options.rationale: A fully managed plan with no control-plane fee and two small instances replaces the 3-node cluster, with autoscale trimming night capacity.
tradeoffs: Less flexible than Kubernetes for multi-service or sidecar patterns
Fixed per-instance billing, no scale to zero

meters.product: Azure App Service Premium v3 Plan - Linux
meters.why: Linux P1v3 plan; 2 instances in business hours (~220 of 730 h a month) and 1 otherwise averages ~1.3 to 1.4 instances running all month; no OS change.

options.details: AKS Free tier cluster (no uptime SLA), same workload, EU region
options.rationale: Drops the ~$73/month Standard-tier management fee while keeping Kubernetes; acceptable if the financially backed control-plane SLA isn't required.
tradeoffs: No financially backed control-plane SLA
Lower control-plane scalability limits
Not recommended for strict-SLA production

meters.why: AKS Free tier cluster, one cluster all month; the menu has no zero-cost free-tier management row, so the closest cluster-level meter is FreeTierInfrastructureCost.

options.details: Linux, AKS node pool with cluster autoscaler (min 2, max 3 nodes) so night-time runs on fewer nodes
options.rationale: AMD 'as' v5 is cheaper than the Intel D4s_v5 for the same 4 vCPU/16 GiB, and autoscaling removes a node during quiet hours.
tradeoffs: Slightly different CPU architecture, validate perf
Autoscaler scale-up latency during morning ramp
options.effort_reason: Node pool autoscaling adds tuning on top of existing self-managed VM upkeep, and the team must learn the new scaling model

meters.why: Regular Linux D4as v5; autoscaler min 2, max 3 nodes, assumed 3 nodes during ~220 business hours and 2 otherwise: about 2.3-2.7 nodes on average, using 2.7 as a conservative estimate.

options.details: Linux, AKS node pool, 3-5 nodes via cluster autoscaler, 2 vCPU 8 GiB each
options.rationale: Smaller AMD nodes scale in finer steps, so capacity tracks the business-hours curve and avoids paying for idle 4-vCPU nodes at night.
tradeoffs: More nodes means more pod-overhead/system-pod waste
Needs pod resource requests tuned

meters.why: Regular Linux D2as v5; autoscaler 3-5 nodes, assumed ~5 nodes in business hours and 3 at night: about 3.5 nodes average over the month.

options.details: General Purpose provisioned, 2 vCore, EU region (Gen5/standard-series)
options.rationale: If metrics show 4 vCores is over-provisioned for ~2,000 users, halving vCores halves compute cost.
tradeoffs: Risk of CPU saturation at peak, must validate with metrics
Manual scale needed if load grows
options.effort_reason: Same managed engine at a smaller size; a resize is quick and routine work stays the same

meters.product: SQL Database Single/Elastic Pool General Purpose - Compute Gen5
meters.why: General Purpose provisioned Gen5; generic 'vCore' sku within the '2 vCore' tier is priced per single vCore, so count = 2 vCores, always on (provisioned).

meters.product: SQL Database Single/Elastic Pool General Purpose - SQL License
meters.why: SQL license for 2 vCores (added by code)

options.details: Flexible Server, General Purpose, 2 vCore, 128 GiB storage, EU region; requires app/schema migration
options.rationale: PostgreSQL Flexible Server has no SQL Server licensing component, so equivalent compute is considerably cheaper, if the app can run on PostgreSQL.
tradeoffs: Requires migrating T-SQL schema/code
Only viable if app is not tied to SQL Server features
Migration effort and testing
options.effort_reason: Engine change requires app and schema migration and new skills; flexible server is still managed

meters.product: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server General Purpose Ddsv5 Series Compute
meters.why: PostgreSQL Flexible Server General Purpose Ddsv5 (D2ds_v5), the 2 vCore compute meter is per-vCore priced at 0.212/h for 2 vCores per its row; assumed per-vCore pricing, count 2, billed all month; no HA required for original-style pricing, but requirements do not demand a standby.

options.details: Standard tier, 6 GB, replicated, no clustering/persistence/VNet injection, EU region
options.rationale: Standard keeps a replicated primary/replica with SLA at a fraction of Premium P1 cost when Premium-only features are unused.
tradeoffs: No clustering, data persistence, or VNet injection
Max 6 GB at this size, check cache size need

options.details: Standard tier, 1 GB, replicated, EU region
options.rationale: For ~2,000 users a 1 GB cache is likely sufficient, and Standard C1 is far cheaper than Premium P1 (6 GB).
tradeoffs: Only 1 GB memory and lower throughput/connection limits
No Premium features (persistence, clustering, VNet)

options.details: Standard tier, 2.5 GB, replicated primary/replica, Linux
options.rationale: Standard keeps the replicated cache but drops Premium-only features that a ~2,000-user web API cache rarely needs, at a fraction of the P1 price.
tradeoffs: No VNet injection, persistence, clustering or geo-replication
Public endpoint plus firewall or private link instead of VNet injection
Lower SLA features than Premium; no zone redundancy
options.effort_reason: Managed cache with the same client; a tier change and connection-string check

meters.why: Standard C2 cache (2.5 GB, replicated primary/replica) is a whole-cache meter; one cache, provisioned so billed all month despite lower night load.

rejections.reason: The Free AKS tier has no financially backed API server uptime SLA, which is not appropriate for a production Web API serving about 2,000 users.

plans.name: Cheapest
plans.summary: Moves everything to Sweden Central, replaces AKS and its VM nodes with Container Apps, switches SQL to PostgreSQL and Redis to Standard C2. This is the lowest-cost combination, but it needs the most migration work.
tradeoffs: Container Apps replaces AKS and the worker VMs (c2 is dropped), so manifests must be rewritten and Kubernetes-level control is lost
SQL to PostgreSQL needs a T-SQL schema and code migration and only works if the app is not tied to SQL Server features
Redis Standard C2 drops VNet injection, persistence, clustering and zone redundancy
Region move from westeurope requires a data migration, though data stays in the EU
plans.note: Moving everything to swedencentral saves $52.21/mo (11.9%) more than staying in westeurope. Plan for the data migration and check latency for your users.

Azure Container Apps / Standard Memory Active Usage

plans.name: Balanced
plans.summary: Keeps AKS and SQL Database but uses an autoscaling D4as_v5 node pool, a 2 vCore SQL database and Redis Standard C2 in Sweden Central. Most of the saving comes from SQL right-sizing and cheaper compute, without changing platforms.
tradeoffs: Halving SQL to 2 vCore risks CPU saturation at peak, so validate with metrics first
Autoscaler adds scale-up latency in the morning ramp and the AMD nodes need a quick performance check
Redis Standard C2 loses VNet injection, persistence and zone redundancy
Region move needs a data migration, though data stays in the EU
plans.note: Moving everything to swedencentral would save only $47.31/mo more (4.6%), not enough to justify a region migration, so this plan stays in westeurope.

plans.name: Safest
plans.summary: Stays in westeurope with the same AKS, SQL Database and Redis Premium, changing only the node pool to autoscaling D4as_v5 so nights run on fewer nodes. It is the smallest change and still saves money with low risk.
tradeoffs: Savings are modest because SQL and Redis stay at their current sizes
Autoscaler scale-up latency in the morning ramp, and the AMD CPU architecture should be validated
No data migration or region change needed

SQL Database Single/Elastic Pool General Purpose - Compute Gen5 / vCore

suggestions: Buy 1-3 year Reserved Instances or an Azure Savings Plan for the D4s_v5 nodes and the SQL vCores (roughly 30-55% off); reserve a baseline of 2 nodes if load is steady.
Enable the AKS cluster autoscaler and scale the node pool to 1-2 nodes at night/weekends (or use a spot node pool for non-critical pods); consider smaller D2s_v5 nodes if CPU usage is low.
Switch SQL Database to the serverless General Purpose tier with auto-pause (or scale down vCores) if usage is idle at night, and use Azure Hybrid Benefit if you have SQL licenses.
Downsize Redis from Premium P1 to Standard C1/C2 (about 1/3 the cost) unless you need clustering, persistence or VNet injection; keep everything in West Europe or North Europe for EU residency.

suggestions: Buy 1-3 year Reserved Instances or an Azure Savings Plan for the D4s_v5 nodes and the SQL vCores (roughly 30-55% off); reserve a baseline of 2 nodes if load is steady.
Enable the AKS cluster autoscaler and scale the node pool to 1-2 nodes at night/weekends (or use a spot node pool for non-critical pods); consider smaller D2s_v5 nodes if CPU usage is low.
Switch SQL Database to the serverless General Purpose tier with auto-pause (or scale down vCores) if usage is idle at night, and use Azure Hybrid Benefit if you have SQL licenses.
Downsize Redis from Premium P1 to Standard C1/C2 (about 1/3 the cost) unless you need clustering, persistence or VNet injection; keep everything in West Europe or North Europe for EU residency.
